scenario: [LNUL.4.2]'s `and`, all nine cells over {true, false, null}: true only for (true, true); false wherever an operand is false, null included on the other side; null for (true, null), (null, true) and (null, null). One P fact holds t = true, f = false and n = null. Each cell `a and b` is two rules: `and_ab` fires only when the cell is true, and `and_ab_not`, `not (a and b)`, fires only when it is false, so a null cell fires neither. So `and_tt` and the `_not` rules of the five false cells fire, and `dead_rules_expected` requires the rest never to. A runtime answering `false and null` with null misses `and_fn_not` and `and_nf_not`. One answering `true and null` with false fires `and_tn_not`. One with no null fires one rule of each null pair. Agenda order is source order ([LDET.5.4]). Path: nothing hoists (no conjunct compares a slot with a literal). Under a `not`, the `and` is an expression: libds's rete/eval.c BINOP arm for DS_RETE_BINOP_AND, Mercury's ds.eval.lnul_4_2_absorbing with `false` deciding. A top-level `and` may instead be emitted as the node's tests, combined by the same absorbing `and` ([IRET.7.6]), so the plain rules and the `_not` rules between them reach both forms.
